monthly_review.summary: You've increased running intensity and efficiency this month, trading volume for higher-quality efforts — evidenced by faster pace, higher HR, more Z3–Z4 time, and improved cadence and aerobic efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: Your aerobic efficiency improved by +0.37 (13.42 → 13.79) despite higher average HR and faster pace — indicating meaningful neuromuscular and cardiovascular adaptation.

goal_tracker.message: You need 5.1 more km across 2 remaining sessions to match last month’s volume — e.g., one 3.0 km easy run and one 2.1 km Zone 2 tempo run.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.79 while avg pace improved and avg HR increased — confirming better oxygen utilization per unit of work, likely due to recent Z3 efforts (25% of time vs 19% last month).

insights.title: Strategic shift toward threshold training
insights.body: Z3+Z4 time increased from 22% (19% Z3 + 3% Z4) last month to 40% (25% Z3 + 15% Z4) this month — a clear progression toward lactate threshold development, supported by your 6:32/km best pace (392 sec/km) in a recent session.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff under fatigue
insights.body: On your longest run (11.1 km at 9:17/km), stride length was 69.7 cm and cadence 153 spm; but on your fastest run (3.0 km at 6:32/km), stride jumped to 91.1 cm with cadence at 162 spm — showing adaptive form under speed stress, though vertical oscillation also rose to 8.4 cm (+0.7 cm), suggesting slightly less economical force application at high intensity.

insights.title: Low-intensity recovery run underutilized
insights.body: Your slowest recent run (10:50/km, 112 bpm) had the lowest cadence (145 spm) and longest ground contact (344 ms), yet it’s the only session with HR clearly in Z1 — however, it contributed just 1.6 TE and may be too short (3.2 km) to fully stimulate recovery physiology; Z1 runs ideally last ≥45 min at <125 bpm for recreational runners.

recommendations.action: Do a 45-minute Zone 1 run tomorrow at HR ≤125 bpm (target pace ~11:30–12:00/km) — use your 2026-06-19 run as baseline but extend duration and lower intensity.
recommendations.reason: Your only true Z1 effort this month was just 3.2 km and 1.6 TE; longer Z1 builds capillary density and promotes parasympathetic recovery without adding fatigue.

recommendations.action: Repeat a 3.0 km interval session next week: 3 × 1.0 km @ 6:32/km (392 sec/km) with 90 sec walk/jog recovery, keeping cadence ≥160 spm and vertical oscillation <8.0 cm (use your 2026-06-11 run as pacing model).
recommendations.reason: This pace is your current best and aligns with Z4 intensity (confirmed by 144 bpm HR and 3.4 TE); repeating it with focus on form metrics will reinforce neuromuscular patterning.

recommendations.action: Add 10 seconds of cadence-focused drills (e.g., high-knee march, butt-kicks) pre-run before your next two runs — especially before the 3.0 km intervals — to prime neuromuscular coordination and support your recent cadence gains (146 → 151 spm).
recommendations.reason: Cadence increased +5 spm this month and correlates with improved efficiency; targeted priming helps sustain that adaptation under fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Build on your recent Z3–Z4 volume increase by reinforcing pace–HR–form relationships at lactate threshold, while protecting recovery with one fully restorative Z1 session.
suggested_sessions: 11 km long run @ 9:15/km (Z2–Z3 crossover, HR 138–142 bpm)
